title: AMD Launches Helios AI Rack System as Microsoft Expands Azure Partnership
excerpt: AMD's first rack-scale AI platform delivers 2.9 exaFLOPS per rack with 72 MI455X GPUs, while Microsoft adds three new Azure VM offerings powered by the system.
body:
• AMD has launched Helios, its first rack-scale AI system with 72 MI455X GPUs, directly challenging Nvidia's dominance in data center AI infrastructure.
  • Microsoft is integrating Helios into Azure with three new VM offerings for AI inference, data processing, and electronic design automation.
  • Helios delivers 2.9 exaFLOPS of FP4 compute and 31 TB of HBM4 memory per rack, using open Ethernet-based interconnects instead of Nvidia's proprietary NVLink.
  • AMD CEO Lisa Su will detail the Helios production timeline at the Advancing AI 2026 keynote in San Francisco on July 23.

AMD's Rack-Scale Gambit

Advanced Micro Devices has entered production with Helios, the company's first fully integrated rack-scale AI platform, marking the most significant challenge to Nvidia's data center dominance in over a decade. The system, built around AMD's Instinct MI455X GPU on the CDNA 5 architecture, houses 72 accelerators in a single double-wide rack capable of delivering 2.9 exaFLOPS of FP4 inference compute.

The MI455X chip packs 320 billion transistors across chiplets manufactured on TSMC's 2nm process node, making it among the first GPUs at that manufacturing frontier. Each GPU carries 432 GB of HBM4 memory — 50% more than Nvidia's competing Vera Rubin offering — giving Helios a total of 31 TB per rack, enough to run trillion-parameter models without partitioning across multiple systems.

Microsoft Bets Big on AMD

Microsoft announced it will deploy Helios across Azure's cloud infrastructure through three new virtual machine offerings. The ND MI455X v7 VMs will handle production-scale AI inference for reasoning, search, and agentic workloads. Azure HDv2 VMs, co-designed with AMD, will tackle AI data preparation and agent coordination with nearly 500 physical 6th Gen EPYC cores, 4 TB of RAM, and 32 TB of local NVMe storage. Azure HXv2 VMs will target electronic design automation and scientific computing with 176 cores clocked above 5 GHz.

"Engineering teams are pushing the limits of simulation, chip design and scientific computing. At AMD, we experience those demands firsthand as we design future AMD EPYC CPUs and AMD Instinct GPUs."

— Mark Papermaster, Executive Vice President and CTO, AMD

The Azure expansion reflects Microsoft's broader strategy of building a heterogeneous AI infrastructure rather than relying on a single chip supplier. The company continues to work with Nvidia while also developing its own custom silicon, positioning AMD as a critical third pillar in its compute stack.

Open Standards vs. Nvidia's Lock-In

AMD's most deliberate strategic differentiator is Helios's open-ecosystem design. The platform uses the OCP Open Rack Wide standard co-developed with Meta, and employs UALink-over-Ethernet for GPU interconnects rather than Nvidia's proprietary NVLink. This means data center operators can source networking hardware from competitive suppliers rather than being locked into a single vendor.

The tradeoff is real: Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers higher training throughput at 2.5 exaFLOPS versus Helios's 1.4 exaFLOPS at FP8, and its NVLink 6 interconnect offers advantages for mixture-of-experts model architectures. But AMD's memory capacity advantage makes Helios compelling for inference-heavy deployments, which now account for the majority of AI compute demand.

The Customer Pipeline

Beyond Microsoft, AMD has secured commitments from OpenAI for a 6-gigawatt infrastructure deployment, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure for 50,000 MI455X GPUs starting in Q3 2026, and Rackspace Technology for 30 megawatts of compute capacity through 2028. HPE and Supermicro have announced Helios-based systems of their own.

Engineering samples and limited-volume Helios production are targeted for H2 2026, with mass-production ramp expected in early 2027. AMD CEO Lisa Su is expected to provide sharper shipment timelines and potentially new hyperscaler design wins at the Advancing AI 2026 keynote on July 23 in San Francisco.

What It Means for the Indian Tech Workforce

The AMD-Microsoft partnership has implications beyond Silicon Valley. India's chip design ecosystem is deeply embedded in both companies — AMD's Hyderabad and Bangalore centers employ thousands of engineers working on EPYC and Instinct architectures, while Microsoft's new India South Central Azure region in Hyderabad is targeted for completion in mid-2026. For the estimated 300,000-plus Indian engineers working in the U.S. semiconductor and cloud computing sectors, the expansion of AMD's AI infrastructure business represents growing career opportunities across design, validation, and deployment.
